claims.claim: Reviewers note that additional packs and add-on content are expensive.

citations.review_text:
Despite what Steam, will tell you I have played Sims 4,in some way, since 2015 have too many hours to count. I stopped play cause EA is one of if not the worst company in game, and they stopped listening to the ones of us who genuinely loved playing the game. 

Some positives:
       -It's now free to play
       -The community is still active, is mostly people that have been here for a minute, and (if you wish) make CC (mods) that can new and fun stuff not available in the "stuff packs"
       -DLC of all types go on sale often


The Cons:
       -Unfortunately everything else is overpriced or just not worth buying
       -Most DLC packs (unlike the expansion packs and stuff packs) are stuff that was in the base game of Sims 2 & 3 
       -The Expansion and Stuff packs are all but required to enjoy the game 
       -EA decided that the house and doll game needed a "battle pass" that some times can give you a reskin of an item that you can't use because you don't own the related stuff pack/kit


Sadly the happy memories and years of playtime of this game do not equals a recommendation for me.
Have over 1k hours on EA. Heavily recommend playing with mods. If not, then it's alright but add-ons are expensive.

Cannot recommend due to the people / company that own the game.
Basically a giant cash grab making everything a pay add-on. Seriously disappointing. I love sims, dedicated sims 2 & 3 player until recent couple of years.

You can not only customise the physical appearance of your character, like their face and body.

I especially love how you can make individual outfits for every occasion, it lets you really express that character with how they dress to impress.

Dear individuals that inhabit this platform, 
I dearly recommend this game for it offers great entertainment, amazing character customisation and with the right mods, you can even have your poor sims killing one another. Thank you for your attention, dear readers, and let us speak more at another time.
Yours truly,
Peggy am Main

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the base game as lacking in content without purchasing downloadable content.

citations.review_text: I would not recommend this game unless you love capitalism and are part of the problem. This game ruined my life and made me poor. The base game is good and all, but it doesn't have much to offer unless you buy DLC. Not to mention how expensive the DLC is. As of November, 2026, it would cost you at least $1000 to have most of the DLC, just for the game to be entertaining enough to play. Its almost like Minecraft but worse, you have a two week's straight of gameplay and then abandon it for the rest of the year. I've roughly spent $130 on this game and haven't touched it since July 2023. I now regret pouring that money into this game and I wish I could've spent it on something better.

You'd think after 485 hours just on pc and 200 more on console, I'd have MUCH to say. Up until recently it would've been no. Now that patches slowed down and mods aren't breaking 24/7, its very fun. People who "Dont get the fun" just didn't have any DLC. It IS sad that base game is so lacking but I'm a EA whale; I've bought every pack (non-kit) at least once across platforms. 
With that credibility on my back, I say the sims 4 is a Mid-at-worst but Amazing-at-best life simulator game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game relies heavily on mods and custom content to remain engaging or complete.

citations.review_text: Realistically, the core game is a buggy mess that has been under developed and over-monetized by EA, but it is made whole by the incredible modding community. Because of their hard and often thankless work, this game remains a wonderful base for story and world building where you can truly create anything your heart desires.

I have played TS4 for years now on multiple platforms such as PS4/PS5 and XBOX, but PC absolutely takes the cake with not one, but 5 cherries on top. Though EA as a company sucks, and I don't recommend giving EA any of your money, thankfully with the base game now being free-- MODs and CC are your best friend here, and make the game feel so much more complete, I could never ever go back to console. You don't even need a stellar PC for this game, for the most part a half-decent laptop will do so long as your RAM is more than just 8GB. TS4 has come a long way, I've grown up w/the Sims franchise and I hope maybe in the future I'd be more willing to give EA my money again one day.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily monetized with an abundance of expensive expansion packs and downloadable content.

citations.review_text: I would not recommend this game unless you love capitalism and are part of the problem. This game ruined my life and made me poor. The base game is good and all, but it doesn't have much to offer unless you buy DLC. Not to mention how expensive the DLC is. As of November, 2026, it would cost you at least $1000 to have most of the DLC, just for the game to be entertaining enough to play. Its almost like Minecraft but worse, you have a two week's straight of gameplay and then abandon it for the rest of the year. I've roughly spent $130 on this game and haven't touched it since July 2023. I now regret pouring that money into this game and I wish I could've spent it on something better.

Absolutely brilliant game. There’s something endlessly entertaining about having your own little virtual world where you can build houses, create stories, and watch everything descend into complete and utter chaos. One minute you’re enjoying a perfectly peaceful family life, and the next someone’s been struck by lightning, a marriage has spectacularly fallen apart over some utterly ridiculous drama, or a Sim has decided that setting the kitchen on fire is a perfectly reasonable way to prepare dinner. Marvellous stuff.

That being said, the increasingly shameless monetisation is genuinely impressive. Between the endless expansion packs, game packs, stuff packs, kits, and now Moola, I’m beginning to suspect the real simulation here is what it feels like to be financially ruined. At this rate, I wouldn’t be surprised if EA introduced a 9.99€ expansion pack that allows your Sims to breathe oxygen, with an additional 4.99€ kit for the privilege of exhaling...

Older Sims games, like Sims 3 somehow managed to offer considerably more content even in their sole basegame without charging you the equivalent of a small country's national debt for the luxury of owning a functioning virtual household. Nowadays, wanting the complete experience feels less like buying a video game and more like applying for a mortgage, except the bank gets your money and you get three new hairstyles, a decorative plant, and the ability to do laundry. What an absolute bargain.

And yet, despite EA's apparent determination to extract every last cent from my bank account, I absolutely adore this game and always find myself coming back. It’s ridiculous, chaotic, endlessly entertaining, and apparently my favourite form of voluntary financial suffering LMFAO

10/10 virtual dollhouse. 2/10 financial decisions. 11/10 commitment to daylight robbery.
